input.brief: A desktop benchmark tool that scores local AI agents on open datasets and publishes a global leaderboard

style.name: Framed sheet
style.basis: 6 screens: a developer platform overview, an analytics overview, an events analytics tab, a list detail, a reports dashboard, a flow builder
style.idea: The app chrome is one tinted L-shaped frame; the work sits on a white sheet with a hairline edge and soft corners, so depth comes from a single tone step and no shadow.
style.colourBudget: under 3%; the brand shrinks to the logo and a 2px tab underline, the data carries the chroma

font.second: IBM Plex Mono, for IDs and keys only
font.note: KPI values at 400; the semibold goes on the label and the active tab.

style.signature: One tinted frame holds the sidebar and the 48px top bar with no rule between them; the page is a white sheet inset 8px from the window's right and bottom edges, with a 1px edge, 16px corners and no shadow. The active tab is a 2px underline in ink or the accent; everything else in the chrome is grey.
identity: The frame tinted from the product's colour in place of #f9fbfc: one low-chroma step of its hue (a green-grey for a climate or farm tool, a blue-grey for an observability tool, a stone for a print shop). The sheet stays white.
The brand's own hue from the brief as --chart-1 in place of the dealt teal, on the main series and the one selected state, at 3:1 or more on white, never violet or indigo.
IBM Plex Mono for IDs, keys and the figures in tables (one job): its figures have their own drawing, and a developer reads them as the product's.
avoid: a border between the sidebar and the top bar
cards whose border is heavier than the sheet's (#cdcfcf on cards read as heavy in the study)
a fourth nesting level: frame, sheet and card are enough
different gutters for the KPI row and the chart row (20 against 24 was flagged)
style.notes: The study's second data hue in this style was an orange (#e88e46) that falls inside the house terracotta range; the third chart colour here is an amber moved out of that range and darkened to 3:1 on white.

shell.name: Tinted frame, white sheet

numbers.sheetInset: 8px from the window's right and bottom edges (12 and 16 once each)
numbers.topBar: 48px on the chrome ground with no rule; search 548x32 centred on the window with a shortcut hint
numbers.floatingVariant: both panels inset 12px with a 12px gutter, radius 10

shell.blueprint: Sidebar and top bar share one tinted ground with no rule between them, forming an L; the page lives on a white sheet. Variant one: the sheet butts against the sidebar and the top bar and is inset 8px from the right and bottom edges, 16px radius, 1px edge. Variant two: a flush L-frame with no inset, the frame marked by one rule. Variant three: sidebar and content are two floating panels inset 12px from every edge with a 12px gutter. The top bar, when present, is 48px and holds a centred search, the account button and a help or AI icon. Inside the sheet the content has 24px padding and starts with the breadcrumb or title row.
shell.phone: The frame disappears: the sheet becomes the screen, with a 48px top bar (menu button, title, one action) on the chrome tint. The search moves into the menu sheet or behind an icon.

pattern.name: KPI strip, main chart and a side rail
pattern.basis: a newsletter home; a community overview
pattern.blueprint: Title row: a 24px noun or the product's name at 600-700, an optional 14-16px grey line under it, and the one primary action on the right, bottom-aligned with that line. 16-24px below, the scope row: section tabs and the date range in one row of 32-36px controls, or a 48px segmented track with the range select inside its right end. Then a grid of 1fr and a fixed 384px rail with a 24px gap. Main column: one KPI container split by 1px dividers into 3-5 equal cells (14px grey label, 24px value at 400-600, a 12px caption naming the baseline and window), then the main chart card, which is the largest thing on the screen, then the next card, all 16px apart. Rail: 16px headings outside their cards, 8px above each and 16px after the previous card; a recent-items list of 3-5 rows on a 45px pitch with 1px rules, closed by a 30px outlined 'View all' button instead of pagination. The rail starts level with the first card, not with the title.
pattern.phone: The rail moves below the main column; the KPI container becomes a 2-column grid; tabs scroll inside their own row.

pattern.name: Object header and a six-column grid
pattern.blueprint: The page header is the object itself: one card (88px, 14px padding) holding a 50x62 cover, the 18/600 name with 28px icon buttons beside it (open, copy, share), a 13px grey meta line (date, time, place) and outlined 36px actions on the right. Under it, underline tabs on a full-width 1px rule, then a 36px row with a segmented time range on the left and a refresh button on the right. The body is one 6-column grid with one gutter (14px) in both directions whose spans change by row while every edge lands on the same lines: 3 KPI tiles of 2 columns, the main chart in 4 columns beside a side chart in 2, two progress cards of 3, a full-width trend of 6. Give the widest card to the screen's question, and do not give 824px to one ring and one legend row (flagged).
pattern.phone: The header card keeps cover, name and meta, with actions in a kebab; every grid item takes the full width in the same order.

pattern.name: Settings in two columns
pattern.basis: one settings page; stacking from a narrow rail card. The basis is thin.
pattern.blueprint: A centred column of about 1152px. Each section is one row: a label column of about 450px (16/500 title, 14px grey description; the title's cap top 6-8px below the panel top, level with the panel's first line) beside a panel of about 700px with a #fafafa fill, 16px radius, 16px padding, no border and no shadow. Sections are split by a full-width 1px rule with 32px above and below. Inside a panel: field labels 14/500 above 40px white inputs (1px #e8e8e8, radius 10), 8px from label to field, 16px between fields, 24px from the description to the first label, 16px to the Save button; switch rows with a 14/500 title, a 20px status badge 8px after it, a 14px grey description and a 28x16 toggle 16px from the right edge, centred on the title line. A plan-gated feature shows a 48px tinted strip with a 32px button directly above its panel, and the panel stays readable. When a panel runs much taller than its label, put the section's help or a summary of the current values in the label column rather than 250px of nothing.
pattern.phone: Each section stacks: title and description, then the panel at full width. Inside, label, 8-10px, field, 16-26px to the next pair; toggles stay on the right of their title.
